patient_overview.name: Arlie Farrell
patient_overview.description: Arlie Farrell is a 72-year-old white man who still works full-time doing overnight security shifts, living with ischemic heart disease, high blood pressure, and chronic low back pain. He's anxious and quick to apologize, often bracing himself as if he's about to be scolded for his eating habits or missed doses. He tends to steer the conversation away from anything that makes him feel exposed, especially around reading labels or following written instructions. A dietetics student will need patience and gentleness to get past his deflections and reach what's really going on with his day-to-day eating.

demographics.occupation: Overnight security guard at a retail distribution warehouse
demographics.residence: Holiday City-Berkeley, New Jersey; household of 4
demographics.cultural_context: Arlie grew up in a working-class family in rural New Jersey and left school after his GED to start working right away, a point of quiet pride for him. He never married and has spent much of his adult life in physically demanding jobs where eating was something squeezed in between tasks, not planned around. His church community, which he's attended for over twenty years, is the closest thing he has to family, and the potluck dinners there are some of the only home-cooked meals he gets.

secondary_diagnoses: Abnormal findings diagnostic imaging heart+coronary circulat
medical_history: Abnormal findings diagnostic imaging heart+coronary circulat since 1998
Urinalysis with reflex to microscopy and culture (2025-12-17)
current_symptoms: Dull, aching low back pain that flares after standing for long stretches at work
Occasional chest tightness he describes as 'a weird squeeze' that comes and goes
Stuffy nose and post-nasal drip most mornings
Fatigue, especially toward the end of his overnight shifts
Occasional dizziness he attributes to 'just getting older'
clinical_findings: Mild forward-leaning posture and slow, careful movements consistent with chronic low back pain
Appears tired, with faint dark circles, consistent with irregular shift-work sleep
Nasal congestion and mouth breathing with a slightly hoarse voice from chronic sinusitis
Mild midsection fullness consistent with BMI in overweight range

medications.name: Hydrochlorothiazide 25 MG Oral Tablet
medications.adherence: Mostly consistent, but admits he sometimes forgets on busy shift days
medications.patient_concerns: Worried it makes him need the bathroom too often during his shift, so he sometimes skips it before work

medications.name: Acetaminophen 325 MG / Oxycodone Hydrochloride 10 MG Oral Tablet [Percocet]
medications.frequency: As needed for pain, up to twice a day
medications.adherence: Takes it sparingly because he's afraid of 'getting hooked' and only uses it when the back pain is unbearable
medications.patient_concerns: Scared of the stories he's heard about painkillers like this one, keeps asking if he's taking too much

medications.name: Ibuprofen 400 MG Oral Tablet [Ibu]
medications.frequency: As needed, usually with meals when his back flares
medications.adherence: Fairly regular when pain is bad, otherwise skips it
medications.patient_concerns: Worries it's hurting his stomach since he sometimes takes it on an empty stomach from the vending machine run

medications.name: lisinopril 10 MG Oral Tablet
medications.adherence: Consistent, keeps it next to his coffee maker as a reminder

medications.name: amLODIPine 2.5 MG Oral Tablet
medications.adherence: Inconsistent; forgets evening dose often when working late shifts
medications.patient_concerns: Mentions his ankles sometimes swell and wonders if the pill is 'not working right'

medications.name: Acetaminophen 300 MG / Hydrocodone Bitartrate 5 MG Oral Tablet
medications.adherence: Uses only on his worst back pain days, tries to avoid it because he confuses it with the other narcotic pill
medications.patient_concerns: Afraid of taking the wrong pain pill combination and overdosing by accident

medications.name: Clopidogrel 75 MG Oral Tablet
medications.adherence: High; takes it with his lisinopril because 'the nurse told me to pair them'
medications.patient_concerns: Worries about bruising easily but hasn't mentioned it to his doctor

medications.name: Simvastatin 20 MG Oral Tablet
medications.patient_concerns: Doesn't understand why he needs it since 'my numbers were fine last time'

medications.name: 24 HR metoprolol succinate 100 MG Extended Release Oral Tablet
medications.adherence: Consistent on days off, less so during long shift stretches when he loses track of time
medications.patient_concerns: Feels more tired since starting it and isn't sure if that's normal

medications.name: Nitroglycerin 0.4 MG/ACTUAT Mucosal Spray
medications.adherence: Carries it in his jacket pocket but rarely uses it, afraid of 'setting something off' by using it wrong
medications.patient_concerns: Nervous about spraying it incorrectly since the instructions on the box are hard for him to follow

supplements_and_otc: Store-brand antacid tablets kept in his truck
Saline nasal spray for his sinus congestion
A multivitamin his sister bought him that he takes 'when I remember'

nutrition_profile.dietary_pattern: Irregular, driven by overnight shift schedule; heavy reliance on vending machines, gas station food, and fast food drive-throughs between midnight and 6 AM
food_preferences: Likes salty snacks like pretzels and chips because they're 'easy and don't go bad'
Enjoys his church's potluck casseroles and baked ham on Sundays
Prefers coffee loaded with cream and sugar to stay awake on shift
Dislikes most vegetables except canned corn and green beans
foods_or_behaviors_to_explore: Frequent purchases of candy bars and sugary soda from the break room machine during overnight shifts
Skips meals during the day then eats a large, heavy dinner before his shift starts
Relies on fast food value menus (burgers, fries) on the drive home at 6 AM
Rarely reads nutrition labels on packaged snacks, often guessing at sodium or sugar content
nutrition_profile.meal_pattern: Skips breakfast most days since he sleeps through mid-morning; small lunch; large dinner before his overnight shift; grazes on vending machine snacks through the night
nutrition_profile.hydration: Drinks a lot of coffee and some soda; rarely drinks plain water unless reminded
nutrition_profile.physical_activity: Walks the warehouse floor during shifts but otherwise sedentary; back pain limits exercise on days off
nutrition_profile.substance_use: Never smoked tobacco; audit-C alcohol score of 0, essentially does not drink
nutrition_profile.sleep: Disrupted, irregular daytime sleep due to overnight work schedule, often only 5-6 hours

psychosocial_profile.personality: Anxious, apologetic, braces for criticism before it comes, tends to downplay his own struggles
psychosocial_profile.communication_style: Soft-spoken, apologizes frequently ('sorry, I know that's bad'), changes the subject when a topic feels too uncomfortable, especially around reading or understanding instructions
goals: Keep working as long as his back allows
Avoid another trip to the ER for his heart
Feel less tired during his shifts
Stay in good standing at his church, including helping with the Sunday meal setup
concerns: Worried the student or dietitian will scold him for his vending machine habits
Afraid his heart condition will get worse and he'll lose his job
Embarrassed that he doesn't always understand nutrition labels or his medication instructions
beliefs: Thinks pain pills and heart pills are the 'real' treatment and food is just extra
Believes he should already know how to eat better at his age and feels ashamed he doesn't
Thinks his tiredness is just a normal part of being 72 and working nights
motivations: Wants to keep working to support himself and not depend on anyone
Wants to stay active enough to keep helping at his church
Fear of ending up like a coworker who had a heart attack on the job
fears: Having a heart attack during a shift and being found too late
Being seen as 'not smart enough' to understand his own care
Losing his place at church if he becomes too sick to attend
Being lectured or judged for his eating habits
barriers: Overnight shift schedule limits access to fresh food
Chronic back pain makes cooking and standing at a stove difficult
Low health literacy makes labels and instructions confusing, which he hides out of embarrassment
Limited household income makes fresh produce feel like a luxury
strengths: Shows up reliably for work despite pain and fatigue
Deeply committed to his church community and its potlucks
Willing to listen when something is explained simply and without judgment
Has gone this long without smoking or drinking, showing capacity for discipline
psychosocial_profile.support_system: A close-knit church congregation he's been part of for over twenty years, including a pastor who checks in on him and a few older members who bring him meals when his back is bad; limited contact with family
psychosocial_profile.readiness_to_change: Contemplation; knows his eating and medication habits aren't ideal and sometimes feels scared enough to want to change, but isn't sure where to start and worries he'll fail

initial_information: He works nights as a security guard and eats 'whatever's around' during his shift
He has heart trouble and high blood pressure and takes 'a bunch of pills'
His back pain has been going on since 2014 and sometimes it's really bad
He mentions his church family a few times, says they're 'like my people'
discoverable_information: With gentle questions, he'll describe his vending machine and drive-through habits in more detail
He'll admit he skips breakfast most days because he's asleep
He'll mention he drinks a lot of coffee to stay awake on shift
He'll say he sometimes forgets his evening blood pressure pill when work runs long
reluctant_information: If asked directly and kindly, he'll admit he gets confused by the directions on his pill bottles and sometimes just guesses the timing
He'll reluctantly share that he mixes up his two pain medications sometimes because the names look similar to him
hidden_information: Arlie cannot reliably read the nutrition facts panel on packaged food and has never told any provider this; he nods along and pretends to understand rather than ask
He has gone to the ER once in the past year for chest tightness he never reported to his regular doctor because he was embarrassed about missing work

opportunities.learning_objective: Assess health literacy and adapt nutrition education materials accordingly
expected_discoveries: Arlie struggles to read nutrition labels and medication instructions but hides this through nodding and deflection
He prefers verbal, simple explanations over handouts with numbers and percentages
possible_patient_reactions: He gets quiet and says 'I think I get it' without really understanding
He changes the subject to his back pain when asked to read something aloud
He visibly relaxes when the student offers to go through a label together instead of handing it to him

opportunities.learning_objective: Explore shift-work eating patterns and identify realistic meal timing strategies
expected_discoveries: His biggest nutrition risks come from the overnight vending machine runs and the heavy pre-shift dinner
He has little control over his break schedule, limiting meal planning
possible_patient_reactions: He laughs nervously and says 'I know it's not great, I'm sorry'
He brightens when asked what snacks might work better for his truck or locker
He worries aloud that any changes will be 'too much to keep up with' on his schedule

opportunities.learning_objective: Use motivational interviewing to meet him in the contemplation stage without triggering shame
expected_discoveries: He wants to change but is scared of failing and being judged
His church community could be a source of support and accountability if invited in gently
possible_patient_reactions: He apologizes repeatedly before admitting he's scared about his heart
He opens up more when the student validates his effort instead of listing problems
He mentions wanting to ask his pastor for support once he feels less ashamed

opportunities.learning_objective: Reconcile a complex polypharmacy regimen with nutrition and lifestyle counseling
expected_discoveries: He confuses his two opioid-containing pain medications and sometimes doubles up unintentionally
He takes hydrochlorothiazide inconsistently due to bathroom access concerns during shifts
possible_patient_reactions: He looks embarrassed and says 'I probably shouldn't tell you that'
He asks if the student can write things down in simpler terms for him
He expresses fear about taking too much pain medication by accident

opportunities.learning_objective: Identify and strengthen the patient's existing support systems for behavior change
expected_discoveries: His church potlucks and congregation members who check on him are a significant source of both food and emotional support
He has limited contact with biological family, making the church his primary support network
possible_patient_reactions: He lights up talking about church, a clear contrast to his anxious tone elsewhere
He says he'd be willing to bring healthier dishes to potlucks if someone showed him how
He worries his church friends would judge him if they knew how he really eats at work

assumptions: Arlie's ischemic heart disease and hypertension are longstanding and managed primarily through medication with limited past nutrition counseling
His full-time overnight work is physically tolerated despite his age and back pain due to financial necessity
The household of four likely includes roommates or family members he does not consider close support, consistent with his limited social contact score
His chronic pain management with both ibuprofen and two opioid combination medications suggests a complex, possibly poorly coordinated pain regimen
optional_details: He keeps a small cooler in his truck for snacks but rarely stocks it with anything beyond soda and leftover Halloween candy
He was taught to drive a forklift decades ago and still mentions it with pride
He has a habit of jingling his keys when he's nervous during conversations
